first.rationale: Current data shows activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 demonstrates that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to their first meaningful action. This directly addresses the activation decline. While memory_31 and memory_86 show onboarding simplification also works, activation_messaging is the more targeted intervention for the acute activation drop and can be deployed faster than structural onboarding changes. Verification of memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding) will confirm whether the prior onboarding improvements are still holding or have degraded, which informs whether activation messaging alone will suffice or if compound intervention is needed in future weeks. Standard experiment scale balances risk against the immediate competitive pressure from new entrant pricing. This preserves the option to pivot if results disappoint while maintaining focus on sustainable qualified revenue over churn-inducing promotional pricing.

final.rationale: Archive confirms memory_31 (signup simplification) lifted SMB activation +9% with +4% qualified revenue but showed -1% retention risk. Archive confirms memory_86 (shortened onboarding) improved completion +13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention +3%. Given the 4% onboarding completion decline QoQ, memory_86's proven retention benefit makes it attractive, but the current 6% activation drop is more acute and less explained by onboarding flow alone. Memory_91 (activation messaging) directly targets the engagement gap without the retention trade-off risk seen in signup simplification. Running activation_messaging as a standard experiment this week addresses the immediate activation decline, compounds well with either onboarding optimization or promotional pricing in future weeks, and preserves long-term qualified revenue by avoiding unsustainable pricing pressure. The activation messaging lever is lower-risk and faster-deploying than structural onboarding changes, leaving future capacity to address the onboarding completion decline or competitive pricing threat.
